step3_model_comparison.note: SMOTE generates synthetic minority patients to rebalance classes.
Non-linear interactions plus built-in feature importances.
Interpretable baseline; balanced class weights lift recall.
Models P(x|y) then inverts it with Bayes' rule.

step3_selection.rule: models within 0.01 F2 of the best are treated as tied; the tie is broken by out-of-fold recall, then by a fixed interpretability/deployability priority list

step3_thresholds.rule: maximise recall subject to precision >= 0.50; cost model FN=5 x FP=1

step3_synthetic.note: Deployed model. Re-weights real patients; generates nothing.
Naive baseline - the minority class is simply outnumbered.
Interpolates on the straight line between a patient and a neighbour.
Statistical generator: per-feature marginals joined by a correlation matrix.
Conditional GAN: a generator learns to fool a critic that sees real patients.
Variational autoencoder: encodes patients to a latent space and samples from it.

step3_calibration_comparison.note: The deployed threshold is tuned on the forest's raw out-of-fold scores, so the raw scores stay the decision variable; calibration is reported so a displayed percentage can be read honestly.

step5_revalidation_protocol: Collect a labelled Indian cohort (both sexes, 20+ years) with the same eight measurements and a confirmatory OGTT / HbA1c as the label.
Score it with the frozen pipeline - no refitting, no re-imputation statistics - and report recall, precision, AUC and calibration with bootstrap intervals.
Check feature shift first: Indian patients develop diabetes at lower BMI, so the BMI-risk relationship learned on Pima women may not transfer.
Re-tune only the threshold on that cohort's out-of-fold scores against the same recall-first rule, then re-check the precision guard at Indian prevalence.
If calibration slope or AUC degrade materially, refit on the new cohort and treat Pima as pre-training, not as the deployed model.

Glucose.label: in the diabetic range on a 2-h OGTT

BMI.label: obese by Asian-Indian cut-offs, overweight by WHO
